transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15 09:32 UTC
Duration: 52 mins (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sara Whitman (Zenith - Head Cloud Eng), Pranav Kapoor (Zenith - Head Compliance), Lina Gomez (Zenith - Platform Security)

Summary: quick discovery to map regulatory constraints and deployment fit (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for a planned pilot. Emphasis on EU residency for some data, HIPAA-adjacent personal health-like data from employee benefits, strict audit/logging needs, and key residency/KMS requirements.

Topics: deployment modes, key management and key residency, log retention & redaction, SOC 2 / HIPAA evidence, network isolation (VPC/on-prem), rolling fallbacks, latency vs cost, benchmark plan

-- Transcript --
[00:00:12] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We, um, appreciate you taking the time. Quick round-robin — can folks confirm names and roles?
[00:00:20] Sara (Zenith): Sara Whitman, head of cloud engineering, hello.
[00:00:23] Pranav (Zenith): Pranav Kapoor, compliance — hi.
[00:00:26] Lina (Zenith): Lina Gomez, platform security.
[00:00:29] Diego (Redwood SE): Diego Ruiz, solutions engineer on the inference team.
[00:00:31] Maya: Great. We planned 45, put aside a bit more. Goal: figure out constraints for a pilot and which deployment model looks feasible — hosted, dedicated, or private.

[00:01:05] Sara: high level — we're building a customer-facing insights product, some PII and EU-customer data will get touched; also a small stream of employee benefit claims which have health-adjacent info. Our legal folks flagged both GDPR and HIPAA-ish concerns, so we need to map what stays in-region and audit trails.

[00:01:40] Pranav: timeline is Q1 pilot, production by Q3 if everything lines up. Primary blockers are: key residency (we cannot have keys leave EU for certain data), long-tail audit logs for 7 years for some records, and demonstrable SOC2 / ISO type controls. Also SSO and RBAC to integrate.

[00:02:05] Maya: ok, thanks. Quick question — which cloud regions are you using today and do you have any on-prem footprint?
[00:02:12] Sara: primary infra in Azure eu-west-1 and aws eu-central-1; we have a small on-prem vault cluster in Amsterdam for secrets. We do, um, store some long-term logs in our retention blob.

[00:02:38] Diego: that helps. On the Redwood side, examples: Hosted (fastest onboarding) runs in our public regions — we do have EU regions, but with Hosted the control plane and some telemetry may be multi-region depending on tenancy. Dedicated gives you customer-isolated GPU pools — capacity reserved — and Private is a VPC/private control plane or on-prem option where we can localize control plane and logs.

[00:03:10] Pranav: can you be precise on where the keys live in each mode? For compliance we need to show key custody — ideally customer-managed KMS with keys staying in EU.
[00:03:20] Diego: Sure — Hosted: default is Redwood-managed keys (encrypted at rest with our KMS). We can offer customer-managed keys (CMKs) in some tiers but Key residency is tricky with Hosted because the control plane may call KMS across regions; we typically suggest Dedicated or Private for strict key residency.

[00:03:44] Lina: So Private would allow us to bring our own KMS? HSM?
[00:03:47] Diego: Yes — Private supports BYOK with customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. We can connect to your on-prem HSM via a trusted gateway or integrate with cloud KMS confined to the EU region. There are some network setup steps — will need a dedicated peering and VPN or direct connect.

[00:04:10] Sara: And logs — we need to keep full request/response traces for 7 years, redacted for PII, and we need proof that redacted data was removed, not just hidden. How do you present audit artifacts?

[00:04:26] Maya: We have audit logs that can be exported to S3/Blob and retained under your retention policy. For Hosted we can provide logs but they may include metadata about model version; for Dedicated/Private you get more control and you can configure log forwarding and retention lifecycles. On redaction — we can do configurable log redaction at ingestion and provide hashed identifiers instead of raw PII.

[00:04:50] Pranav: hashing is ok, but we need to show the process in attestation; also chain of custody — who touched the keys and when.

[00:05:02] Diego: Our audit trail includes key-usage logs if you're on CMK/BYOK — those come from the KMS logs (Cloud KMS or HSM vendor). In Private you'll have direct access to those logs. In Dedicated we can also forward KMS operations to your logging account. Hosted can be negotiated but not default.

[00:05:26] Lina: How about model input retention? If we do prompt caching for latency, are prompts stored? What's TTL?

[00:05:35] Diego: We do prefix/KV cache to speed up autoregressive workloads — default is short TTL (minutes) to reduce token cost, but that is configurable. For compliance use-cases, we recommend disabling persistent cache for regulated workloads or setting TTL to zero; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. Hosted default is cached short-term and anonymized.

[00:06:00] Sara: Any difference in SLOs — for us latency is 200-400ms p50 for short prompts; cost is also a factor.

[00:06:10] Maya: Dedicated targets predictable throughput and latency, that's why many banks pick it. Hosted is more bursty and cheaper per-testing, Private gives you full predictable SLAs but requires longer setup and higher baseline. Tradeoff is cost vs time-to-market.

[00:06:34] Pranav: security attestations — do you have HIPAA BAAs? SOC2 Type II? ISO 27001?

[00:06:40] Maya: We are SOC2 Type II compliant and have ISO 27001 coverage; we can share the summary and redacted reports under NDA. For HIPAA, we provide a BAA for Private and Dedicated customers on enterprise contracts — Hosted BAAs are available for certain enterprise accounts but require review.

[00:07:00] Lina: Any prior bank customers? We need references that did similar residency and retention work.

[00:07:06] Maya: Yes, we have several financial services customers on Dedicated and Private; will share references and a case study.

[00:07:20] Diego: Technical note — when you do canary rollouts and model versioning, the runtime supports KV cache invalidation and automatic fallback to smaller model variants if latency or capacity issues happen. Important for graceful degradation.

[00:07:40] Sara: About data flow — we need to diagram where data persists: raw prompts, embeddings, logs, models' KV caches. Do you have recommended diagrams we can start from?

[00:07:50] Maya: yes, we'll send a data flow template. For sensitive data, our recommendation is: 1) don't persist raw prompts; 2) store redacted traces and hashed identifiers; 3) use BYOK for keys; 4) push logs to your own storage with lifecycle policies.

[00:08:20] Pranav: One more — chain of custody for model updates. If you push a model that regresses on PII scrubbing, we need a rollback and audit trail.

[00:08:29] Diego: The platform supports pinned model versions and rollouts (canary, A/B). We also run automatic evals against regression sets; Dedicated/Private customers can supply their eval sets and get alerts on quality regressions. Rollback is configurable per-route.

[00:08:51] Lina: Network isolation specifics — can Redwood run entirely inside our VPC so egress never leaves the VPC except to model weights or is there a control plane hop?

[00:08:59] Diego: Private can run with a private control plane in your VPC, so control plane calls stay in region. For Dedicated we can set up VPC peering but some control plane telemetry may transit Redwood-managed endpoints; we can minimize that and sign data processing agreements. Hosted will always have some control plane outside customer VPC.

[00:09:28] Sara: For the pilot, we probably want to trial Dedicated in eu-central-1 and see if Dedicated can meet latency and retention needs. If not, we'd evaluate Private.

[00:09:36] Maya: that makes sense. Diego, can you outline a benchmark plan?

[00:09:40] Diego: Sure. Plan: 1) we take a representative traffic trace (you can sanitize PII), 2) run a 2-hour soak at expected QPS plus 2x burst, 3) measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and model KV cache hit rates. We'll also run a variant with cache disabled to measure worst-case. We can stream logs into your S3 and compare retention/size.

[00:10:05] Pranav: will that show key usage logs and KMS ops?

[00:10:09] Diego: Yes if you enable CMK and we forward KMS logs to your logging account. For Hosted we'd need a workaround and limited visibility.

[00:10:22] Sara: How do you handle data subject access requests (DSARs) under GDPR? If a user asks for deletion, do prompts and embeddings get removed?

[00:10:31] Maya: We support deletion workflows. For Hosted we can attempt deletion from our indices but need coordination. For Dedicated/Private, you control the storage and can run purge jobs. Embeddings stored in vector index can be rehydrated and we can provide deletion scripts — but it's important to map which artifacts persist and where.

[00:10:56] Lina: Are embeddings reversible? This is a legal question but technically we need to know risk.

[00:11:03] Diego: Embeddings are generally not reversible to full PII reliably, but we treat them as sensitive. For high-risk data we recommend not embedding raw PII; instead use hashed tokens or pseudonymization pre-processing.

[00:11:22] Pranav: Ok. Regarding contractual SLAs: what uptime and RTOs do you offer in Dedicated and Private?

[00:11:29] Maya: Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime for cluster availability (we'll provide exact percentages in the SLA — typical is 99.9% for service availability). Private depends on the deployment and is negotiated; our enterprise contracts include runbooks and support windows.

[00:11:48] Sara: Do you support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning?

[00:11:52] Diego: Yes — SSO (SAML or OIDC) and SCIM provisioning are supported across Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SSO too but provisioning is limited in self-serve tiers.

[00:12:05] Maya: wondering if there are any blockers from your side we should surface now?

[00:12:10] Pranav: Key thing is we need evidence of key residency and KMS logs, plus a BAA for HIPAA-ish workloads. Also a clear policy for log redaction and the ability to push logs to our storage without Redwood retaining an extra copy.

[00:12:28] Lina: Also encryption at rest must be AES-256 and certs managed, plus HSM-backed CMKs for the most sensitive classes.

[00:12:36] Diego: All standard. For HSM-backed CMKs, we have integrations with cloud HSMs and can do on-prem connectors. We'll include specifics in the architecture doc.

[00:12:48] Sara: Do you charge extra for BYOK/HSM?

[00:12:50] Maya: There's typically enterprise add-on fees for private networking and managed HSM integrations — we'll include a rough TCO in the pricing sketch.

[00:13:02] Pranav: One more question on data residency: our EU customers' data must not leave the EU even in transient caches. Does Private fully guarantee that?

[00:13:12] Diego: Private deployed inside your EU VPC with local model weights and a private control plane will keep everything in-region. We can document the network paths and provide a region-lock attestation. Dedicated can be region pinned but occasionally depends on global control plane ops; we can negotiate operational constraints.

[00:13:38] Sara: Are there examples of how you handle logs that may contain sensitive data? Do you redact at the agent before sending?

[00:13:45] Diego: We support pre-ingest redaction rules in our SDKs and at the API gateway — you can mask or hash fields before they are written to the log. For Hosted customers we run a sanitization pipeline but recommend customer-side redaction for strict compliance.

[00:14:02] Pranav: Ok. Let's talk about evidence — to satisfy our auditors we need a short bundle: SOC2 summary, BAA template, network diagram, KMS integration notes, and an explanation of log retention and purge.

[00:14:18] Maya: We'll package that up and can share under NDA.

[00:14:22] Diego: also, on the technical side, I'll attach a sample dedicated config that shows how to set up CMK, VPC peering, and log sinks to S3 with lifecycle rules.

[00:14:35] Sara: For the pilot, expect a sanitized trace of about 5k requests/hour with average prompt length of 120 tokens. We need to see cost per 1k tokens and latency impact of caching.

[00:14:49] Diego: Perfect. We'll simulate that in the Dedicated benchmark and show token cost and p95/p99.

[00:14:56] Pranav: If we go to Private later, how long is setup?

[00:15:00] Maya: Private can take 8-12 weeks depending on network approvals and on-prem HSM provisioning; Dedicated pilot can be short — couple weeks to get reserved capacity.

[00:15:10] Lina: Are there personnel reqs on our side? Dedicated/private need an infra owner and network person.

[00:15:16] Maya: yes, small ops involvement, we'll need your network/security and a project sponsor.

[00:15:24] Sara: I want to surface a question from legal: can Redwood sign a clause that guarantees no access to raw prompts by internal staff for certain routes?

[00:15:33] Maya: We have internal access controls and RBAC, plus audit logs. For stricter cases we can add contractual clauses and technical measures (encryption and key controls). We'll need legal review.

[00:15:46] Pranav: competitor question — we also spoke to Vendor X (cohere-ish) who said they do everything in-region in EU Hosted. How do you differentiate?

[00:15:55] Maya: Differentiator is we offer dedicated and private deployments with operator-managed runtimes and explicit routing policies, plus economics tooling. We'll share case studies and the differences in control plane exposure.

[00:16:10] Diego: On the tech side, our runtime offers continuous batching and optimized kernels to reduce cost while preserving latency. It matters at scale for token economics.

[00:16:22] Sara: Ok, let's move to recap and next steps.

[00:16:30] Maya: Recap: Pilot in Dedicated in eu-central-1, run benchmark with sanitized trace, provide SOC2/BAA docs, architecture and TCO sketch, and attach dedicated config. Action owners: Diego for benchmark playbook, Maya for pricing and docs, Pranav to confirm regulated fields.

[00:16:55] Pranav: We'll get the sanitized trace and a list of regulated fields by next Friday.

[00:17:02] Lina: I'll coordinate the network people for peering.

[00:17:06] Diego: I'll send the runbook and sample config.

[00:17:09] Maya: Any other questions?
[00:17:11] Sara: Not on my side.
[00:17:12] Pranav: no. Thanks.

[00:17:18] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc bundle and next steps.

[00:17:25] -- End of call notes, recording stopped but meeting lasted 52 mins according to system --
